rationale: Closed the last sampling limitation of the split-brain chain by turning the healed phase into a long run: the harness now commits 200 further entries on the healed leader before sampling and reports how many entries followed the conflict index. Local construction feedback over both restart modes shows the window is substantial (202 and 212 entries after healing) and that the defect-mode state is unchanged by it: the restarted node still reports {A,B,C}, the entry at the conflict index is still inconsistent across nodes and its FSM still holds the minority write, while the feature-off control run stays consistent and reports {A,B,C,D,E}.

scope.description: The two-mode five-node restart scenario (feature-on restart and feature-off control in one execution) with the healed phase extended into a long run of 200 further committed entries before the sample.
assumptions: All state is produced by normal operations: bootstrap {A,B,C}, election, committed applies, a user snapshot on A, AddVoter D and E, graceful restart of A with and without the feature, transport partition, healing and further committed entries.

The long run is applied on the healed leader whichever node it is; in the feature-on run that leader may be the stale node, in which case its own configuration decides which peers receive the entries, which is recorded through the per-node log indexes.
The sample is taken after the leader's log has advanced at least 150 entries past the conflict index, with a 15s bound; the derived long_run_exercised operand states whether that happened.
Exact indexes are not asserted; the comparisons use the mode-conditioned structural operands.
excluded: No crash, on-disk store or user Restore is exercised.
The long run commits ordinary command entries only; no further membership change is made during it.

experiment.prefix: The helper builds five InmemTransports in a full mesh with per-node InmemStore, InmemCommitTrackingStore and InmemSnapshotStore and Config with TrailingLogs 0, bootstraps {A,B,C} from A, starts A, B and C with MockFSM and the feature enabled, elects a leader, transfers leadership to A if needed, applies three commands, waits for A to apply, takes a user snapshot on A, starts D and E, adds each as voter, applies one further command and emits 'fixture'. It shuts A down, cuts {A,C} from {B,D,E}, reconnects A to C only, restarts A with the mode's feature setting and emits 'restart'. It waits for a leader in each partition, applies one write on each leader, reads the entries at the shared index and emits 'outcome'. It reconnects the mesh, waits for one leader, applies one more entry, then applies 200 further entries on that leader and waits (bounded by 15s) until the leader's log has advanced at least 150 entries past the conflict index; only then does it sample payloads and terms at the conflict index, differences in the applied write lists, each node's configuration and the long-run operands, and emit 'healed'. A repair phase follows as before: choose a current-configuration leader, cut A off, apply ten commands, snapshot the leader, reconnect A, wait for the snapshot install and emit 'repaired'. The test runs mode defect_restart first and control_no_restore second. Event order: fixture, restart, outcome, healed, repaired, fixture, restart, outcome, healed, repaired.
semantic_changes: After the mesh is reconnected and one entry is committed, the harness applies 200 further entries on the healed leader, waits until the leader's log has advanced at least 150 entries past the conflict index, and then samples.
The healed event reports long_run_error, entries_after_heal and the derived long_run_exercised operand.
experiment.responsibility: hashicorp/raft configuration scan with the RestoreCommittedLogs replay, and the AppendEntries duplicate-skip that prevents later replication from repairing the divergent entry or refreshing the configuration.

comparisons.description: Feature on, after ~200 further committed entries: all nodes should hold the same entry at the conflict index.
Feature on, after the long run: the restarted node should use the committed configuration.
Operand: the sample really was taken after at least 150 entries past the conflict index.
Operand: the restarted node kept receiving entries, so the persistence is not a stalled node.
Feature off control after the same long run: entries should be consistent.
Feature off control after the long run: the restarted node should use the committed configuration.

experiment.revision_reason: Adds a long run of 200 further committed entries before the healed sample and reports the number of entries after the conflict index, so the persistence of the stale configuration and of the divergent entry and applied state is observed after substantial progress rather than after one entry; the scenario phases and the earlier comparisons are otherwise unchanged.
